Replay

Coordinator-driven game rooms

8 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Transition behaviorRecovery measurementsRemaining M5 workExternal checkpoint dependenciesDisplaying backup preparation

Use Room(State, Control, Action, Event, Seats) when a game needs coordinator-approved authority and host migration. It combines an authenticated coordinator client, a time-limited authority lease, independently owned prepared checkpoints, and the gameplay Session. It runs initial hosting/joining, periodic trusted backups, planned handoff, abrupt takeover, old-owner rejoin, and surviving-client redirection.

Dedicated infrastructure rooms keep authorities and standbys avatarless through bootstrap, failover and return; authenticated member identity is independent of a playable seat.

Gameplay can use native ENet or authenticated RTC. The control connection can use ENet or WebSocket (control_backend = .Websocket, with a full URL in coordinator). For RTC, set session.backend = .Rtc and session.rtc.url to the trusted signaling provider. Room derives the authority-specific room code from the verified view and supplies its challenged authorization callback. Member IDs/keys/game tokens remain provisioned. Browser Room instances use the paired clock and Godot cryptographic nonces. It obtains fresh process incarnations through the registration handshake.

Odin
options := replaygd.Room_Options{
    identity = provision.identity,
    key = provision.control_key,
    room = provision.room,
    coordinator = provision.coordinator_address,
    control_port = provision.control_port,
    bootstrap = provision.bootstrap,
    session = replaygd.SESSION_OPTIONS,
}
options.session.network = game_network_config
options.session.token = player_game_token
options.session.replication.accept_checkpoints = true // trusted successor opt-in
options.successor = provision.successor
options.successor_seat = provision.successor_game_seat

error := replaygd.room_open(&room, initial_frame, model, options)
// Every frame: room_frame, then consume changes from room.session.
error = replaygd.room_frame(&room, delta_seconds, controls)
count := replaygd.session_changes(&room.session, changes[:])
frame, valid := replaygd.session_state(&room.session)

Gameplay still uses the same typed controls/actions/model. room_issue sends an action, and room_handoff requests a planned transfer. Dispose with room_close. room_save requests a durable service checkpoint; optional automatic publication runs in room_frame alongside the existing lease and migration work. Trusted Party members can also resume published progress from a fresh process when no live authority remains, using a new fenced grant. Runtime owners remain at stable addresses; models/immutable asset descriptors must remain valid across role changes. A selected successor receives complete authority data. The room does not choose arbitrary peers or grant hosting permission itself.

Transition behavior#

The coordinator's authenticated live view determines the endpoint and epoch. Clients reconnect their gameplay transport while retaining their runtime and old action/presentation ledgers. A lower restored connection generation is valid in a new epoch; old-epoch traffic remains rejected. Initial joins still require a valid Welcome before exposing a world. A recovering client can retain its previous frame for presentation until the new checkpoint arrives.

net.client_authority quarantines outstanding actions. The new authority's durable received/settled frontiers classify each old ID as Applied, Rejected, Retained, Retired, or Settled_Unknown. Retained commands await the authority's verdict; unreplicated commands are not blindly retried. New sequence numbers start from the recovered ledger, so losing an old suffix does not create a permanent sequence gap. The epoch distinguishes newly issued IDs from retired ones. Unconsumed outcomes and presentation changes must be drained before changing authority.

The low-level client exposes client_recovery; Session captures its latest report and increments recovery_serial. A promoted client also receives reconciliation against the prepared checkpoint. The old owner retains its local pending ledger when becoming a client, so its new Welcome resolves those IDs too.

Presentation resets close retained old-epoch effects with Cancel changes, including confirmed continuous effects. They do not replay the new checkpoint's historical cosmetics. Applications should treat cancellation of an already-finished one-shot as harmless and derive ongoing world presentation from the current frame. Counters or action UI keyed by sequence must include epoch; Cavecrawl now does this. These cosmetic resets do not implement an external persistent-effect outbox.

Planned handoff waits for local queued commands to settle, then freezes gameplay with a phase-aware permit while retaining control-plane renewal of the owner's lease. The frozen owner drains unadmitted gameplay traffic so a full primary queue cannot block checkpoint acknowledgments on the shared transport. Neither draining nor renewal advances the world or admits new commands. Once the successor has prepared the exact acknowledged final point, the owner retires its lease and release/claim establishes the newer epoch. The old host can then rejoin as a player. The phase gate is reinstalled after runtime replacement for subsequent handoffs. Successor loss or a failed final transfer stops renewal and enters fenced owner recovery; it does not resume the retired epoch. In-flight accepted remote commands are explicitly retired by this profile's restore policy; their IDs and verdicts remain accounted for. Abrupt takeover uses the latest owned, coordinator- accepted checkpoint after lease expiry.

A transition checks its lease after Room's initial preflight. If a valid clock reaches the deadline between those checks, Room keeps the old runtime/prepared checkpoint, marks gameplay fenced and waits for fresh authenticated control progress. It does not extend that deadline, reset the lease clock or count the transition as complete. Poisoned clocks and unrelated failures remain fatal. Redirect, old-owner rejoin, takeover and published-checkpoint installation use this handling. See the transition-expiry regression.

Room.phase, control_error, and the underlying Session's fenced state describe progress/failure. The driver keeps the control connection alive while gameplay is fenced and retries disconnected transports. A surviving owner that loses its lease may request a new epoch from the coordinator using its retained world, provided no successor has already won. This never revives the expired epoch. A granted successor renews its reservation while it finishes installing the runtime/presentation.

Recovery measurements#

A rejected Claim returns the driver to Following so it can prepare newer replicas. Retrying the same rejected point would prevent preparation from making progress even while checkpoint transfer continued. last_command/last_result retain the latest completed coordinator decision, and claim_rejections/busy_claims count rejected attempts. These diagnostics are distinct from control_error, which reports local RPC/control operations. Coordinator fencing and rollback limits are unchanged; a failed claim does not make an old archive eligible or establish authority.

examples/replay_quickdraw/early_claim_run.sh injects an early signed claim while the owner is live, requires a Busy response followed by a newer prepared point, then kills the owner after tick 600 and checks continued combat. The controlled failure before the fix froze preparation at sequence 2 while transfer advanced to sequence 72. Both normal and gameplay-fault runs pass after the change.

Room.recovery reports source/destination epochs, the actual approved checkpoint tick, previous locally confirmed tick, known lost ticks, archive bytes, and observed protocol interruption. install_us measures elapsed wall time of the successful authority-runtime replacement call, including archive decode and runtime setup; it is not CPU time or total disruption. Takeover can reuse the receiver's existing checkpoint schema cache before releasing the old Session. The checkpoint tick is distinct from the later Welcome tick when the guest finally joins. known_lost_ticks cannot describe work no participant reported; it is not proof that unobserved work was preserved. Interruption is measured from the local recognition of fencing/transition until the replacement is usable, not from an unknowable remote crash time or a physical input-to-display measurement.

Cavecrawl displays reconnect/host-change feedback and notes known rollback. Its four-process gates run coordinator, initial host, trusted successor, and a third guest. The guest loots and opens a door, stays alive through migration, retains its bag, and performs a newly acknowledged action in epoch 2. Planned mode additionally checks that the old host rejoins; crash mode kills it.

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_migration/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_migration/crash_run.sh

Both passed with 120 ms gameplay receive delay on each process. An additional planned run passed with 20 ms jitter, 10% loss, and 10% duplication. Individual receipts included checkpoint 112 / zero known lost ticks / 436 ms local interruption for planned transfer, and checkpoint 101 / six known lost ticks / 558 ms for crash recovery. These are scenario receipts, not latency percentiles or a full comparison. The coordinator explicitly reported Planned versus Abrupt recovery in the matching gates. All original games remain separate.

Quickdraw now exercises the same driver during active hitscan/lob combat:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/migration_run.sh

The successor compares its installed baseline with the exact coordinator-approved frame containing live projectiles, a pending respawn, weapon cooldowns, equipment and collision history. Surviving clients then land fresh historical-query hits, settle a new purchase and compare canonical world digests at a common tick. Planned mode also checks the old host's stable seat and restored mixed presentation policy. The harness separately measures trigger-to-ready time on the same machine, so lease expiry/discovery time is visible alongside Room's narrower interruption metric. The test's two hosting members are explicitly trusted; this does not authorize passing competitive authority secrets to an arbitrary player.

Remaining M5 work#

Replay Slopball additionally exercises planned and crash migration while an owner-streamed RigidBody2D is moving. The successor checks the exact approved world, reseeds pose and momentum, accepts fresh ownership scopes and continues kicking/ scoring. Surviving peers compare whole-world hashes at a common tick. See examples/replay_slopball/migration_run.sh. This restores accepted engine state; it does not replay or transfer Godot solver contact caches.

  • Public room/invite deployment and richer lobby controls; known-member process registration and endpoint rebinding exist.
  • Broader failure timing/topology coverage beyond the tested successor loss, repeated handoff, isolated-host control partition, and returned killed host.
  • Recovery during the remaining combat/loot scenario corpus beyond the initial Cavecrawl and Quickdraw gates.
  • Broader error/retry UX and platform/network reachability coverage. Dedicated-server policy has its own integration gates.
  • External outbox/idempotency integration where games need persistent services.

These gates cover the scenarios described above; the remaining migration and roadmap cases need separate acceptance.

External checkpoint dependencies#

Room_Options.preparation_ready(user, point, bytes) may gate coordinator preparation on external dependencies. It receives an already validated candidate archive as a read-only borrow; it must not mutate it or retain the slice. The application can memoize dependencies by point and service their asynchronous loading outside the simulation. Nil keeps the ordinary checkpoint-only behavior.

An incomplete candidate may be replaced by a newer fully received archive while its dependencies load. This avoids waiting indefinitely on an obsolete candidate. An incomplete newer candidate does not invalidate a previously prepared point. If the lease expires and the service still approves the older point, Room discards the incomplete candidate and claims that approved point. This preserves the stated rollback boundary; it does not claim that unavailable content has been recovered. Applications must retain the dependencies of every point they advertise as prepared.

Displaying backup preparation#

Use the backup-status observation for waiting, transferring, approved, stale and uncertain states. It retains accepted coordinator metadata across pending requests and does not modify authority decisions or permits.
